messages:
maya: quick question — where should the lightweight sanity checks live in the onboarding flow? ingest vs a separate preflight service? thinking about catching bad artifacts earlier but also cost tradeoffs.

oliver: i'd put a very cheap tier at ingest. stop obviously broken payloads before bench. saves compute downstream. but need to be strict about cost. :thinking_face:

ranjit: +1 to ingest but keep them tiny. e.g. checksum/shape, token-distribution sketch, simple kv-cache smoke. detect corruption and big distribution shifts.

lina: distribution drift is tricky — models evolve. we should avoid hard thresholds that cause churn. dynamic baselines (rolling window) would help.

maya: what about a two-tier approach: 1) preflight at ingest (PASS/WARN/FAIL + small signal blob) 2) full bench/validation async with richer metrics and human review on regressions. preflight has to be cheap (<50ms).

oliver: if preflight returns WARN, runtime routing could use a fallback variant? that adds latency but keeps app up. if FAIL, stop intake. tradeoffs there.

ranjit: agree. fallback policy should be per-model config and pluggable. sample config snippet: 

```yaml
preflight:
  latency_ms_budget: 50
  checks:
    - shape_check
    - token_dist_sketch
    - kv_cache_smoke
fallback:
  on_warn: route_to_previous_quantized
  on_fail: block_ingest
  on_timeout: route_to-hosted
```

lina: logging/telemetry question: preflight must emit a tiny vector only — not full inputs — for privacy and storage. something like sanity_signal: [ok, drift_score, kv_ok].

eva: +1. also include a "sanity_signal_version" and attach to model metadata so downstream tooling can interpret uniformly.

maya: SLIs we need to track: false positive rate (warn=>bench-ok), warn->fail cascade rate, additional latency caused by fallback, and cost delta per 1k models.

oliver: interface boundary note: ingest service should own only the boolean/compact signal. bench/validation owns heavy metrics and golden eval. keeps responsibilities clear.

ranjit: canary/rollout interplay — canaries should use stricter preflight configs than broad rollouts. we should support an override flag in model manifest for canary.

lina: agree. also we should version preflight checks so old manifests keep working.

maya: operational playbook: WARN -> autoschedule into quick-bench queue and tag as high-priority; FAIL -> email onboarding owner + block; TIMEOUT -> route-to-hosted fallback and alert.

deploy-bot: ingest preflight hook branch deployed to staging at 1738123600 :rocket:

oliver: nice. i'll write an RFC follow-up that includes: API for preflight results, config schema for fallback, telemetry schema, and proposed SLOs.

maya: i'll review the draft. ranjit + lina can you both please review for edge cases (quantized models, long-context variants)?

lina: ack :+1:

ranjit: ack :thumbsup:

maya: thanks — if possible, mention KV-cache smoke as a separate cheap check (it catches major runtime incompatibilities).

oliver: will do. planning to drop a draft by EOD tomorrow.

maya: sweet.
